summary: A TypeScript library (zero runtime dependencies, node:crypto for every primitive) implementing a simplified, WireGuard-style point-to-point encrypted tunnel, built in two stages (stage 1: handshake, transport, anti-replay, pseudo-TUN over real UDP; stage 2: periodic session rekeying). The handshake is a two-message Noise-IK-style exchange: each peer holds a static (long-term, exchanged out of band like a WireGuard public key) X25519 keypair and a fresh ephemeral keypair per handshake attempt. Session keys are derived via HKDF over three chained ECDH outputs -- static-ephemeral (dhSE), ephemeral-static (dhES), ephemeral-ephemeral (dhEE) -- with separate send/receive keys per direction (i2r/r2i HKDF info labels) so the two directions never share a nonce space. Authentication falls out of ECDH algebra itself rather than a separate signature: DH(a.priv, B.pub) equals DH(b.priv, A.pub) only when both sides hold the real matching keys, so an initiator using the wrong believed static key for the responder fails at the responder (AUTH_FAILED) before any session exists, while a responder configured with the wrong expected key for a real initiator fails differently (UNTRUSTED_PEER) -- the handshake still decrypts but the claimed identity is not trusted. Every transport packet is ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD-encrypted with a monotonically increasing per-session counter as the nonce, tagged with a receiver-chosen id (not the sender's identity or address, mirroring WireGuard's own receiver index) so decrypting an inbound packet is a single map lookup. Anti-replay is an RFC 6479-style fixed-size sliding bitmap (not a growing set of seen counters): a counter is checked for replay BEFORE decrypting (cheap rejection) and recorded as seen only AFTER the AEAD tag verifies (recording an unauthenticated counter would let a forged packet burn a value the real sender has not sent yet -- found by writing it the other way first and watching a dedicated test fail). A tampered ciphertext or auth tag always fails to decrypt and is dropped, never crashes; every receive-side method returns a typed rejection instead of throwing, since it processes bytes from an untrusted network, while send-side methods throw on local misuse (this repo's usual error convention). A TunDevice interface (send/onReceive, the app's view) with an InMemoryTunDevice implementation (plus onSend/deliver, the engine-facing driver side) lets the full encrypt/send/receive/decrypt path run end to end over REAL UDP loopback sockets (via VpnNode) without a kernel device -- a real OS TUN/TAP device needs root, which neither this environment nor the owner's Windows dev machine has, so that integration, handshake-replay/DoS-resistance cookies, NAT traversal/roaming, and carrying real IP packets (payloads are opaque bytes by design) are all explicitly not built, documented honestly rather than silently skipped. VpnNode itself is scoped to one active remote peer at a time (point-to-point), though the underlying Peer class can trust and hold sessions with several named peers at once. Stage 2 adds opt-in periodic session rekeying driven by a new injectable Clock (src/clock.ts: systemClock, ManualClock): PeerOptions rekeyAfterMs (time) and/or rekeyAfterMessages (count) arm Peer.checkRekey(), which reports due peers; VpnNode.checkRekey/startRekeyTimer/stopRekeyTimer actually send the new handshake. Each peer name tracks a current session plus at most one retiring session that keeps decrypting in-flight packets on its own receiverId until a grace deadline (rekeyGraceMs, default 10000); pruning happens automatically inside decryptPacket/checkRekey. Only the original initiator ever rekeys (role recorded once and carried forward); a lost rekey handshake never touches the current session and the stale attempt is abandoned after rekeyRetryMs (default 5000) so it can be retried; every rekey is a brand-new Session with a fresh anti-replay window and counter. 82 tests total (17 in test/rekey.test.ts), including a randomized invariant test (5 seeds x 300 packets over real UDP sockets with simulated reordering, duplication and tampering, asserting every original payload is delivered exactly once with no corruption and every replay/tamper is dropped). Mutation checks: 42 total -- 22 in stage 1 (1 survivor -- a stale pending-handshake entry that would permanently block a later re-handshake with the same peer -- was a real gap, closed with a new test, not a behavior change) and 20 in stage 2 on the rekey logic and timer lifecycle, all caught on the first run.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek chhota, WireGuard-jaisa VPN tunnel banaya hai, TypeScript mein, node:crypto ke sirf primitives use karke. Do peers X25519 se handshake karte hain, static aur ephemeral keys dono, forward secrecy ke liye. Har transport packet ChaCha20-Poly1305 se encrypted hota hai, ek per-session counter nonce ke saath, aur ek RFC 6479-style sliding bitmap replay attacks rokta hai. Real OS TUN device nahi banaya -- usko root chahiye, jo na yeh environment na owner ka Windows machine de sakta hai -- isliye poora encrypt/send/receive/decrypt path real UDP loopback sockets par test hota hai, ek InMemoryTunDevice ke through. Stage 2 mein periodic session rekeying add kiya -- naya session aata hai, purana ek grace window tak in-flight packets decrypt karta rehta hai. 82 tests, 42 mutation checks (22 + 20), ek stage-1 survivor tha jo test se close kiya.
pitch.explain_2min:
'Build your own VPN' is project ka point ek paid VPN (NordVPN/Surfshark) replace karna nahi hai -- point yeh samajhna hai ki ek VPN tunnel ACTUALLY kaise kaam karta hai, black box treat karne ke bajaye. Teen core ideas hain jo yeh project concrete banata hai, aur yeh teen ideas TLS, SSH, aur har secure-channel protocol mein dobara aate hain: ECDH key exchange, AEAD encryption, aur anti-replay windows.

Handshake ek simplified Noise 'IK'-style exchange hai, WireGuard ke exact wire format ka byte-exact port nahi. Har peer ke paas do keypairs hote hain: ek static (long-term identity, out-of-band exchange hota hai, jaise WireGuard public key), ek ephemeral (har handshake attempt ke liye fresh, discard ho jaata hai). Session keys HKDF se nikalte hain teen chained ECDH outputs se -- static-ephemeral, ephemeral-static, ephemeral-ephemeral. Authentication kisi separate signature se nahi aata -- yeh seedha ECDH algebra se falls out hota hai: DH(a.priv, B.pub) sirf tab DH(b.priv, A.pub) ke barabar hota hai jab dono taraf REAL matching keys hon. Galat key use karne wala initiator responder par fail hota hai (AUTH_FAILED), aur ek responder jiska expected key galat configured hai woh ek real initiator ko bhi reject karta hai, par differently (UNTRUSTED_PEER).

Transport mein har packet ek receiver-chosen id carry karta hai, sender ki identity ya address nahi -- isliye decrypt karna ek simple map lookup hai. Anti-replay ek fixed-size sliding bitmap hai (RFC 6479-style), growing set nahi -- O(1) aur bounded memory. Counter check decrypt se PEHLE hota hai (cheap rejection), aur record sirf AEAD tag verify hone ke BAAD hota hai -- warna ek forged packet real sender ka counter 'burn' kar sakta tha.

Real OS TUN device nahi banaya -- root chahiye hota hai, jo yahan available nahi hai. InMemoryTunDevice plus real UDP loopback sockets poora protocol end-to-end test karte hain, bina kernel device ke.

Stage 2 mein periodic rekeying aaya, kyunki ek key ko hamesha ke liye use karna uska exposure unbounded kar deta hai. Trigger time (rekeyAfterMs) ya message count (rekeyAfterMessages) hai, dono opt-in, ek injected Clock ke through. Rekey sirf ek naya handshake hai fresh ephemeral keys ke saath. Mushkil part in-flight packets hain: isliye purana session turant delete nahi hota, 'retiring' ban jaata hai aur apne purane receiverId par rekeyGraceMs tak packets accept karta hai. Sirf original initiator rekey karta hai, aur agar rekey handshake lost ho jaaye toh current session ko kuch nahi hota -- rekeyRetryMs ke baad retry. 82 tests, 42 mutation checks (stage 1 ke 22, stage 2 ke 20), stage 2 mein 0 survivors.
pitch.deep_5min:
Ek packet ki journey, Alice se Bob tak, phir ek replay aur ek tamper attempt.

Trust setup. Alice aur Bob dono apna static X25519 keypair generate karte hain (Peer constructor mein). Out-of-band (jaise WireGuard public keys swap karna), Alice.trustPeer('bob', bob.staticPublicKey) aur Bob.trustPeer('alice', alice.staticPublicKey) call hote hain -- yeh exactly WireGuard config file ka 'PublicKey =' line jaisa hai.

Handshake. Alice initiateHandshake('bob') call karti hai -- ek fresh ephemeral keypair banta hai is attempt ke liye, aur message 1 banta hai: Alice ki apni static public key, ephemeral public key, encrypted (AEAD) ek key se jo dhSE (Alice.ephemeral.priv x Bob.static.pub) se derive hoti hai. Bob yeh message decrypt karta hai apni static private key se -- agar Alice ne Bob ki WRONG static public key use ki thi, decrypt FAIL hota hai turant (AUTH_FAILED), kyunki Bob ki derived key Alice ki derived key se match nahi karti. Agar decrypt succeed hota hai, Bob Alice ki claimed static public key dekhta hai -- agar yeh Bob ke trusted-peers list mein nahi hai, UNTRUSTED_PEER (yeh message 1 decrypt ho gaya tha, par identity trust nahi hui). Trust pass hone par, Bob apna ephemeral keypair banata hai, message 2 banata hai jo teen chained DH terms (dhSE, dhES, dhEE) se HKDF ke through final session keys derive karta hai -- do alag keys, ek har direction (i2r/r2i) ke liye.

Transport. Handshake complete hone ke baad, dono ke paas ek Session hai apna-apna send counter aur receive-side AntiReplayWindow ke saath. Alice tun.send('hello bob') call karti hai -- VpnNode yeh packet encrypt karta hai current send counter ko nonce bana ke, ek receiver-chosen id attach karta hai (jo Bob ne handshake ke time assign kiya tha), aur real UDP socket se Bob ko bhejta hai. Bob ka socket packet receive karta hai, receiver id se Session lookup karta hai (ek map lookup, scan nahi), counter ko AntiReplayWindow.check() se PEHLE verify karta hai decrypt se pehle hi (cheap rejection ek obviously bad counter ke liye) -- phir AEAD decrypt hota hai. Decrypt succeed hone ke BAAD hi counter record() hota hai 'seen' ke taur par -- yeh order crucial hai: agar record pehle hota, ek attacker ek guessed counter wala forged packet bhej ke real sender ka future legitimate packet permanently reject kara sakta tha.

Replay attempt. Koi ussi packet ko dobara bhejta hai (same ciphertext, same counter). Bob ka AntiReplayWindow.check() dekhta hai yeh counter already 'seen' hai, turant reject karta hai REPLAY ke saath, decrypt tak pahunchta hi nahi.

Tamper attempt. Koi packet ka ek byte flip karta hai (ciphertext ya auth tag). AEAD decrypt fail hota hai -- ChaCha20-Poly1305 ka authentication tag khud yeh guarantee deta hai. Bob ka decryptPacket() yeh throw nahi karta, ek typed rejection return karta hai (AUTH_FAILED), kyunki yeh untrusted network se aaya data hai, crash nahi.

Rekey (stage 2). Maan lo Alice ka Peer rekeyAfterMs ke saath bana hai. Alice ka VpnNode startRekeyTimer() se har second checkRekey() chalata hai; Peer.checkRekey(now) dekhta hai ki session ki umar threshold cross kar gayi aur koi rekey pending nahi, aur {peerName: 'bob', reason: 'TIME'} return karta hai. VpnNode ek naya HANDSHAKE_INIT bhejta hai -- exactly pehle wala handshake, fresh ephemeral keys ke saath. Bob response BHEJTE hi naya session install karta hai; Alice response RECEIVE karke. installSession() purana session delete nahi karta -- usko 'retiring' mark karta hai, retireAt = now + rekeyGraceMs, aur woh apne purane receiverId par sessionsByReceiverId mein rehta hai. Toh jo packet Alice ne switch se pehle purani key se bheja tha aur raste mein hai, woh purane receiverId par aata hai aur retiring session usse decrypt kar leta hai, apne alag AntiReplayWindow ke saath. Naye session ka counter aur window 0 se shuru hote hain. Grace khatam hone par decryptPacket() ke andar hi pruneRetiredSessions() usko hata deta hai. Sirf ek retiring generation rakhi jaati hai, sirf original initiator rekey karta hai (role pehle session par record hota hai), aur agar rekey ka HANDSHAKE_INIT kho jaaye toh rekeyRetryMs ke baad pending attempt abandon hokar retry hota hai -- current session bina rukawat chalta rehta hai.

Real TUN device? Nahi -- yeh poora flow InMemoryTunDevice ke through hota hai, jo real UDP sockets use karta hai par kernel routing simulate karta hai. Root chahiye hota real TUN ke liye, jo na yeh environment na owner ka Windows machine provide karta hai -- PLAN.md aur README.md dono mein honestly documented hai.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough: src/clock.ts (stage 2): Clock interface, systemClock (Date.now), ManualClock (set/advance) -- tests time ko bina sleep ke exact boundary par le jaate hain. src/crypto-utils.ts: node:crypto wrappers -- X25519 keygen/ECDH (raw-key JWK import/export), hkdfSync, ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD encrypt/decrypt. src/wire.ts: binary framing for HANDSHAKE_INIT, HANDSHAKE_RESPONSE, TRANSPORT_DATA message types, plus AAD construction har message type ke liye. src/replay-window.ts: AntiReplayWindow -- check() pure hai (no mutation), record() mutate karta hai, dono alag methods isliye hain taaki Session check-before-decrypt aur record-only-after-authenticate kar sake bina ek doosre ka side effect chupaye. src/session.ts: Session -- per-direction keys, send counter (sentCount getter stage 2 ke message-count trigger ke liye), orchestrates check-before-decrypt / record-after-authenticate. src/handshake.ts: do-message Noise-IK-style exchange -- static+ephemeral X25519 keypairs, dhSE/dhES/dhEE se HKDF session keys. src/peer.ts: Peer -- pure protocol state machine (trustPeer, initiateHandshake, receiveHandshakeInit/Response, encryptPacket/decryptPacket). No sockets. Send-side methods VpnError throw karte hain, receive-side methods kabhi throw nahi karte, hamesha typed {ok:false, reason} return karte hain. Stage 2: PeerOptions (clock, rekeyAfterMs, rekeyAfterMessages, rekeyRetryMs, rekeyGraceMs), peerSessions mein har peer ka PeerSessionState (current, establishedAt, role, generation, optional retiring), installSession (rekey par purana session retiring), pruneRetiredSessions, checkRekey + abandonStaleRekeyAttempts, sessionGeneration (sirf observability). src/tun.ts: TunDevice interface (send/onReceive, app-facing) + InMemoryTunDevice (onSend/deliver, engine-facing driver side). src/transport.ts: VpnNode -- ek Peer ko real node:dgram UDP socket aur ek InMemoryTunDevice se wire karta hai, point-to-point (ek active remote peer per node). Stage 2: checkRekey() due peers ko naya HANDSHAKE_INIT bhejta hai, startRekeyTimer/stopRekeyTimer real setInterval manage karte hain, close() timer bhi band karta hai. src/demo.ts: npm run demo, do peers handshake karte hain real loopback UDP par, ek deliberate replay aur ek deliberate tamper dikhate hain reject hote hue, phir ek real rekey traffic chalte hue. test/: 8 files -- replay-window, wire, handshake, session, peer, transport (real UDP), invariants (randomized, real UDP), rekey (stage 2, 17 tests, ManualClock + real UDP).
difficult_decisions: Simplified Noise 'IK'-style handshake, WireGuard ke byte-exact wire format ka port nahi. WireGuard ka real handshake ek timestamp (handshake-replay protection) aur cookie/MAC (DoS resistance) bhi fold karta hai; yeh project woh operational hardening chhod deta hai jo stage 1 ka point nahi hai, aur authentication + forward secrecy ka core shape rakhta hai.

Do keypairs per peer: static (long-term, trustPeer se pinned) aur ephemeral (har handshake attempt ke liye fresh). Session key dono ephemeral private keys par depend karti hai, jo sirf memory mein exist karti hain -- isliye ek later static-key compromise ek EARLIER recorded session ko decrypt nahi kar sakta (forward secrecy).

Receiver-chosen id har transport packet par, sender ki identity ya address nahi -- WireGuard ka receiver index mirror karta hai. Decrypt karna ek single map lookup hai, kabhi scan ya socket-address assumption nahi -- useful hota hai jab NAT ya roaming involved ho, chahe stage 1 ko kisi ki zaroorat nahi.
Anti-replay ek RFC 6479-style fixed-size sliding BITMAP, growing set of seen counters nahi. Fixed memory, O(1) accept/reject -- exactly wahi structure real WireGuard use karta hai.

Counter check decrypt se PEHLE, record decrypt ke BAAD. Check pehle karna ek obviously bad counter par full AEAD decrypt ka cost bachata hai; record baad mein karna crucial hai -- warna ek unauthenticated (forged) counter real sender ka future legitimate packet permanently reject kara sakta tha.

Send/receive ke liye ALAG keys, alag HKDF info labels (i2r/r2i) se. Ek shared key dono directions ke liye matlab dono taraf ke counters ek hi nonce space share karte -- do peers jaise hi ek-ek packet bhej dete, nonce 0 reuse ho sakta tha.

Rekey par purana session turant delete nahi, 'retiring' with a grace deadline (rekeyGraceMs). Dono sides alag instants par switch karte hain (responder response bhejte waqt, initiator response receive karke), aur receiverId-based dispatch ki wajah se old-key packet apne aap purane session tak pahunchta hai -- na wire change, na try-each-key. Bound: maximum ek retiring generation per peer.

Sirf original initiator rekey karta hai. role pehle session par record hota hai aur har rekey par carry forward -- responder manually re-handshake kare tab bhi woh automatic rekey ke liye eligible nahi banta. Dono sides ko rekey karne dena harmless hota, par double churn for zero benefit.
biggest_challenges: P5 mutation survivor: receiveHandshakeResponse apna completed attempt pendingHandshakes se delete karna bhool jaata tha. Replaying message 2 khud harmless tha (same keys re-derive karta, session ko apne aap se overwrite karta) -- isliye koi test yeh pakad nahi payi. REAL consequence alag tha: stale entry ke saath, peer kabhi SECOND handshake start nahi kar sakta tha same name ke saath -- initiateHandshake ka apna 'already pending' guard wrongly old, completed attempt ko dekh ke HANDSHAKE_IN_PROGRESS forever throw karta. Ek naya test add kiya jo assert karta hai ki successful handshake ke baad fresh initiateHandshake kabhi throw nahi karta.

Wrong-static-key scenario do ALAG failure modes mein split hota hai, dono test karna zaroori tha: initiator ki wrong belief (AUTH_FAILED Bob par, message 1 decrypt hi fail hota hai) VERSUS responder ka wrong expected key for a REAL initiator (message 1 decrypt succeed hota hai, par claimed identity trust nahi hoti -- UNTRUSTED_PEER). Dono DH algebra se automatically fall out hote hain, do separate mechanisms nahi.

Randomized invariant test real UDP sockets ke upar simulated reordering/duplication/tampering ke saath likhna -- har originally-sent payload ko InMemoryTunDevice tak EXACTLY once deliver hona prove karna, chahe delivery order kuch bhi ho, aur har duplicate/tampered packet ko never-delivered prove karna, 5 seeds x 300 packets ke across.

Stage 2 ka lost-rekey cleanup sahi scope karna: abandonStaleRekeyAttempts sirf un peers ke pending attempts hatata hai jinka session already hai. Agar yeh first-ever handshake ka pending entry bhi hata deta, toh VpnNode.connect() ke apne timeout se race hoti -- isliye ek dedicated test ('checkRekey does not abandon a pending FIRST handshake') aur mutation RK8. Stage 2 ke 20 mutations sab first run mein caught.
failure_scenarios: Koi packet replay kare (same ciphertext, same counter dobara bhejna): AntiReplayWindow.check() isse 'already seen' dekh ke turant REPLAY reject karta hai, decrypt tak pahunchta hi nahi.
Koi packet tamper kare (ciphertext ya auth tag ka ek byte flip): AEAD decrypt fail hota hai, Peer.decryptPacket() ek typed AUTH_FAILED rejection return karta hai, throw ya crash nahi karta.
Initiator ek WRONG static public key use kare responder ke liye: responder ka message-1 decrypt turant fail hota hai, AUTH_FAILED, koi session nahi banta kisi bhi taraf.

Responder ka khud ka trusted-peers list EK real initiator ke liye wrong key rakhta ho: message 1 decrypt succeed hota hai (initiator ne responder ki real key use ki thi), par claimed identity trust-list mein match nahi karti -- UNTRUSTED_PEER.

Ek handshake message malformed ho (corrupt length, galat type byte): receive-side methods isse throw nahi karte, ek typed rejection return karte hain -- untrusted network data ko process karne ka safe convention.
Same peer ke saath DOBARA handshake karna, pehla successful complete hone ke baad: ab yeh kaam karta hai (P5 fix ke baad) -- pendingHandshakes entry properly cleared hoti hai success par.

Rekey ka HANDSHAKE_INIT raste mein kho jaaye: current session dono taraf untouched rehta hai, traffic chalta rehta hai; rekeyRetryMs ke baad stale attempt abandon hota hai aur agla checkRekey() fresh ephemeral keys se retry karta hai.
Rekey ke beech koi packet purani key se in flight ho: woh purane receiverId par aata hai, retiring session usse decrypt karta hai; rekeyGraceMs ke baad woh id UNKNOWN_SESSION deta hai.
improvements: Real OS TUN/TAP device abhi nahi hai -- root chahiye hota, jo yeh environment aur owner ka Windows machine dono provide nahi karte. InMemoryTunDevice plus real UDP sockets honest substitute hain.

Handshake-replay protection ya DoS-resistance cookie abhi nahi hai -- ek captured HANDSHAKE_INIT replay ho sakta hai (harmless extra attempt banata hai, working session nahi), par koi rate-limit nahi hai repeated attempts ke against. Stage 2 ke rekey handshakes bhi utne hi replayable hain.
64-bit wire counters JS number se model hote hain, bigint se nahi -- exact sirf 2^53 tak. Koi test itne packets nahi bhejta ek session par ki yeh matter kare.
NAT traversal ya endpoint roaming abhi nahi hai -- VpnNode peer ka address pehla packet se seekhta hai aur wahi use karta rehta hai.
Real IP packets carry nahi karta -- payloads opaque bytes hain by design, koi IP header parsing ya routing table nahi.

Rekey ke dauran lost HANDSHAKE_RESPONSE ka test nahi hai: code ke hisaab se responder already naye session par switch kar chuka hota hai, toh responder->initiator packets retry hone tak drop ho sakte hain. WireGuard jaisa key confirmation (responder tab tak purane session par bheje jab tak initiator ka pehla packet naye par na aaye) add karna chahiye, aur rekeyAfterMs mein jitter.

learning_path.concept: ECDH handshake and why authentication needs no separate signature
steps: 1. Concept: do peers X25519 ECDH se ek shared secret derive karte hain bina kabhi private key bheje. Authentication khud DH algebra se falls out hota hai: DH(a.priv, B.pub) sirf tab DH(b.priv, A.pub) ke barabar hota hai jab dono taraf real matching keys hon.
2. Project need: ek VPN ko dono taraf verify karna hota hai ki woh sahi peer se baat kar rahe hain, bina ek alag signature scheme ke complexity ke.
3. Code/API: src/crypto-utils.ts generateX25519KeyPair, ecdh; src/handshake.ts.

4. Detail: wrong static key wala initiator responder par AUTH_FAILED dekhta hai (message 1 decrypt hi fail); wrong expected key wala responder ek real initiator ko UNTRUSTED_PEER dekhta hai (decrypt succeed hota hai, trust fail).
5. Demo: cd projects/24-vpn && npx vitest run test/handshake.test.ts -- 'the initiator using the WRONG responder static key fails at the responder (AUTH_FAILED)'.
6. Interviewer next: agar ek attacker beech mein baith jaaye (MITM), yeh scheme kaise unhe pakadta hai ya nahi?

learning_path.concept: Forward secrecy via ephemeral keys, and the three chained DH terms
steps: 1. Concept: har peer ke paas static (long-term) aur ephemeral (per-handshake, discarded) keypair hai. Session keys HKDF se teen chained ECDH outputs se nikalte hain -- static-ephemeral, ephemeral-static, ephemeral-ephemeral.

2. Project need: agar session key SIRF static keys se derive hoti, ek later static-key leak sab PURANE recorded sessions ko decrypt kar sakta tha. Ephemeral keys sirf memory mein exist karte hain, discard ho jaate hain -- forward secrecy.
3. Code/API: src/handshake.ts (dhSE, dhES, dhEE computation, HKDF).

4. Detail: dhSE sirf initiator ko prove karta hai ki usne responder ki REAL static public key use ki; dhES/dhEE additionally prove karte hain ki initiator khud apni claimed static key ki MATCHING private key hold karta hai.
5. Demo: cd projects/24-vpn && npx vitest run test/handshake.test.ts -t 'ephemeral' -- 'the final keys depend on the ephemeral keypairs'.
6. Interviewer next: agar ek static private key leak ho jaaye, is design mein attacker kya kar sakta hai aur kya nahi?

learning_path.concept: AEAD transport encryption and per-direction keys
steps: 1. Concept: har transport packet ChaCha20-Poly1305 se encrypted hota hai, ek per-session counter nonce ke saath. Send aur receive ke liye ALAG keys hain, alag HKDF labels (i2r/r2i) se.

2. Project need: ek shared key dono directions ke liye matlab dono peers ke counters ek nonce space share karte -- jaise hi dono ne ek-ek packet bheja, nonce 0 reuse ho sakta tha, jo AEAD security completely break kar deta.
3. Code/API: src/crypto-utils.ts chacha20Poly1305Encrypt/Decrypt; src/session.ts Session.encrypt/decrypt.
4. Detail: counter monotonically increase hota hai har send par; ek tampered ciphertext ya tag AEAD decrypt ko fail karta hai, Session.decrypt ek typed rejection return karta hai.
5. Demo: cd projects/24-vpn && npx vitest run test/session.test.ts -- 'a tampered ciphertext byte and a tampered tag byte both fail cleanly'.
6. Interviewer next: agar yeh same key dono directions mein use hoti, exact attack kya ban jaata?

learning_path.concept: Anti-replay: a sliding bitmap, and why check-then-record order matters
steps: 1. Concept: AntiReplayWindow ek RFC 6479-style fixed-size bitmap hai. check() pure hai (koi mutation), record() mutate karta hai -- do alag methods, do alag purpose.
2. Project need: ek attacker captured packets replay kar sakta hai. Fixed bitmap O(1) accept/reject deta hai, bounded memory ke saath, chahe session kitne bhi packets carry kare.
3. Code/API: src/replay-window.ts AntiReplayWindow.check, record; src/session.ts decrypt (check-before-decrypt, record-after-authenticate).

4. Detail: counter check decrypt se PEHLE hota hai (cheap rejection ek obviously replayed/too-old counter ke liye); record SIRF AEAD tag verify hone ke BAAD hota hai -- warna ek forged packet guessed counter se real sender ka future legitimate packet permanently block kara sakta.

5. Demo: cd projects/24-vpn && npx vitest run test/replay-window.test.ts test/session.test.ts -t 'replay' -- 'an exact replay of an already-accepted packet is rejected', 'a forged (unauthenticated) counter is never recorded'.
6. Interviewer next: bitmap ka size (2048 bits default) kis tradeoff ko control karta hai -- bahut chhota hone par kya breaks?

learning_path.concept: Receiver-chosen ids: why packets are not addressed by sender identity
steps: 1. Concept: har transport packet ek RECEIVER-chosen id carry karta hai (handshake ke time assign hota hai), sender ki identity ya socket address nahi.

2. Project need: decrypt karne ke liye jo packet receive hota hai, usse SIRF ek map lookup chahiye (by receiver id), scan ya 'yeh address se aaya hai toh yeh peer hoga' assumption nahi -- yeh NAT ya endpoint roaming ke scenario mein zaroori ban jaata hai.
3. Code/API: src/peer.ts sessionsByReceiverId map; src/handshake.ts (receiver id assignment during handshake).
4. Detail: WireGuard ka real receiver index yahi role play karta hai -- yeh project usi idea ko mirror karta hai bina NAT/roaming khud implement kiye.
5. Demo: cd projects/24-vpn && npx vitest run test/peer.test.ts -t 'session' -- end-to-end handshake aur transport dono directions mein.
6. Interviewer next: agar peer ka IP address mid-session change ho jaaye (roaming), yeh receiver-id design kya karna aasan banata hai?

learning_path.concept: The pseudo-TUN abstraction: testing a full tunnel without root
steps: 1. Concept: TunDevice interface (send/onReceive) app ka view hai; InMemoryTunDevice additionally onSend/deliver expose karta hai, jo VpnNode (engine) drive karne ke liye use karta hai.

2. Project need: real OS TUN device root/admin chahta hai -- yeh environment aur owner ka Windows machine dono ke paas nahi hai. Poora encrypt/send/receive/decrypt path phir bhi REAL UDP sockets par test hona chahiye, sirf 'kernel ne packet route kiya' part simulate hona chahiye.
3. Code/API: src/tun.ts TunDevice, InMemoryTunDevice; src/transport.ts VpnNode.

4. Detail: app sirf send()/onReceive() use karta hai, kabhi nahi jaanta ki doosri taraf kernel device hai ya in-memory stub. VpnNode donon directions ke 'driver' hooks use karta hai actual UDP socket se packets ko tunnel tak deliver karne ke liye.
5. Demo: cd projects/24-vpn && npm run demo -- do peers real loopback UDP par handshake aur exchange karte hain, replay aur tamper dono reject hote dikhte hain.
6. Interviewer next: ek real Linux /dev/net/tun adapter add karna kitna bada change hoga -- kahan isolate hoga?

learning_path.concept: Session rekeying: current + retiring sessions and a bounded grace window
steps: 1. Concept: rekeying matlab periodically ek naya handshake karke nayi session keys lena, taaki koi ek key unbounded time ya traffic protect na kare. Make-before-break: naya session aata hai, purana thodi der 'retiring' rehta hai taaki in-flight old-key packets drop na hon.

2. Project need: stage 1 mein session keys Peer ki poori lifetime chalti thi. Stage 2 opt-in triggers deta hai -- rekeyAfterMs (time) aur/ya rekeyAfterMessages (count) -- aur dono sides ke alag instants par switch karne ke bawajood koi packet lost nahi hona chahiye.

3. Code/API: src/clock.ts (Clock, systemClock, ManualClock); src/peer.ts PeerOptions, checkRekey(now) -> RekeyDue[] {peerName, reason: 'TIME' | 'MESSAGES'}, sessionGeneration; src/transport.ts VpnNode.checkRekey, startRekeyTimer, stopRekeyTimer.

4. Detail: installSession purane session ko retiring mark karta hai (retireAt = now + rekeyGraceMs, default 10000) aur woh apne purane receiverId par reachable rehta hai; sirf ek retiring generation; encryptPacket hamesha current; decryptPacket/checkRekey khud pruneRetiredSessions chalate hain; role pehle session par pin hota hai, sirf initiator rekey karta hai; lost rekey attempt rekeyRetryMs (default 5000) ke baad abandon hota hai; har rekey naya Session = fresh counter aur fresh AntiReplayWindow.

5. Demo: cd projects/24-vpn && npx vitest run test/rekey.test.ts -- 'a packet encrypted on the OLD session right before a rekey still decrypts correctly after the new session exists', 'a lost rekey HANDSHAKE_INIT does not disrupt the still-valid old session, and a later rekey attempt succeeds', aur real-UDP 'packets sent across two rekey boundaries all arrive exactly once, with no corruption'. npm run demo bhi ek rekey dikhata hai.
6. Interviewer next: agar HANDSHAKE_INIT ki jagah HANDSHAKE_RESPONSE kho jaaye toh responder->initiator direction ka kya hota hai, aur WireGuard ka key confirmation isko kaise solve karta hai?

learning_path.concept: Testing honestly: a randomized invariant over real sockets, and mutation testing
steps: 1. Concept: randomized invariant test real UDP sockets ke upar packets bhejta hai with simulated reordering/duplication/tampering, 5 seeds x 300 packets. Mutation check = jaan-boojh ke ek line todo, suite chalao, dekho fail hota hai ya nahi, file restore karo.
2. Project need: handshake x transport x replay x tamper ke combinations haath se likhe tests cover nahi karte poori tarah, aur '82 tests pass' yeh prove nahi karta ki tests kuch pakadte hain.
3. Code/API: test/invariants.test.ts, test/transport.test.ts (real UDP end to end).

4. Detail: Stage 1: 22 mutation checks, 21 first-run caught, 1 genuine survivor (P5 -- stale pendingHandshakes entry blocking a later re-handshake), closed with a precise new test, behavior nahi badla gaya kyunki woh already correct tha for the originally-tested scenario. Stage 2: 20 aur mutation checks (RK1-RK16, TK1-TK4) rekey logic aur timer lifecycle par, sab caught, 0 survivors.
5. Demo: cd projects/24-vpn && npm test (82 tests), aur npx vitest run test/invariants.test.ts.
6. Interviewer next: ek mutation jo 'harmless replay' lage (jaise P5 ka message-2 replay) par ek REAL bug reveal kare kisi doosre angle se -- yeh kaise socho?
